question.text: The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis situated at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from its center is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The magnetic moment of the dipole is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. (Given : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole can be written as

V=μ04πMr2   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required magnetic moment of the dipole.

1.5×10-5=10-7×M20×10-22⇒M=1.5×10-5×20×20×10-410-7⇒M=1.5×4=6 A m2
